# Bind transaction groups across window generations

## Context

A warm reload produces a new `windowId` while the App Worker heap, Workspace instances, and topology may survive. Independent roots of the same app can share one SharedWorker, so `appName` cannot identify a transaction authority. D#18224 resolved four separate coordinates and a token-matched binding lifecycle.

## The Problem

Today `Neo.appsByName[appName]` is an array and fallback lookup selects `[0]`; same-name generations can coexist after reload. Popup/workspace state is connected by consumer-specific URLs and lifecycle hooks. A late disconnect can therefore target the wrong generation, and two independent Workstation roots can collapse into one identity.

## The Architectural Reality

`Neo.manager.Base` is already a collection. A generic `Neo.manager.Transaction` registry matches `manager.Store` / `manager.Window`; its Group children must remain dock-blind. Dock Workspaces register as participants through domain adapters. `appName` stays routing metadata.

## The Fix

Add the collection-backed singleton registry plus generic Group identity/binding lifecycle. Main-thread boot injects a root-minted `groupId`; popups inherit it and carry one `workspaceKey` and spawn `claimToken`; `windowId` is only the replaceable runtime generation. Bindings are `(groupId, workspaceKey) -> {windowId, generationToken}` and unregister only on an exact token match. Duplicate live roots fork; stale popup URLs fail closed.

This increment also moves semantic participant membership into the Group. The existing dock-side `WorkspaceSet` may remain as a domain adapter, but it owns no independent entry map. Its adoption/compensation behavior stays intact until #18312 moves the write protocol; releasing a window binding does not retire its semantic participant.

## Structural Placement

Full structural pre-flight selected `src/manager/Transaction.mjs` plus `src/manager/transaction/` for generic Group support; dock adapters stay under `src/dashboard/dock/`. Update the Runtime Engine inventory because it currently has no `src/manager/` row. No dock imports enter the manager.

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `manager.Transaction` | manager sibling pattern; #18303 | collection-backed Group registry | unknown group returns null/refusal | Architecture Overview + JSDoc | registry unit arms |

| app identity | `Application` / `appsByName` reality | `appName` routes only | never implicit Group identity | ADR | two same-app roots |

## Decision Record impact

Depends on and implements amended ADR 0029.

## Decision Record

Required prerequisite: the #18303 hard-cut ADR leaf.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping

Owns criterion 6 and the binding half of criterion 13; provides criterion 3's first manager ownership cut under the bounded accounting amendment below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `manager.Transaction` registers distinct logical Groups and is exported through the normal manager surface.
- [ ] Root reload retains `groupId`, popup birth/reload inherits it, and an independent same-app root receives a different id.
- [ ] One `workspaceKey` identifies each full Workspace slot; no parallel `workspaceId`/window-slot identity survives without a proven non-1:1 consumer. Group owns semantic participant membership in this increment; any surviving `WorkspaceSet` delegates to that registry and has no independent entry map. Window unbind or binding-lease expiry must not discard a Group that still owns participants.
- [ ] A replacement generation supersedes only the matching `(groupId, workspaceKey)` binding; a late old-token disconnect cannot unbind its successor.
- [ ] A copied Group/slot presented by a second live root forks rather than hijacking; a stale bookmarked popup URL fails closed.
- [ ] The two-Workstation falsifier proves A+popup share one Group, B shares only `appName`, and reloading A touches neither B nor a second Group.
- [ ] The first manager increment carries a measured **implementation code-line** addition/deletion ledger with a **maximum +65 net implementation-line increase** ([explicit author amendment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18309#issuecomment-5551938509)), replacing the original net-negative constraint for this ownership cut. Re-measure the final review head; this is not a general growth exemption. The ledger covers `src/ + apps/ + examples/`, using the repository's Acorn-based `check-file-sizes.mjs` counter. This population covers the engine and both named consumers, Workstation and DemoB; tests, generated assets and documentation do not pay for the increment. Report raw added/deleted lines separately, and identify each replaced parsing/admission/subscription/membership path with its single successor owner; formatting-only or unrelated deletions do not discharge the ownership cut. The shared TearOut identity contract, both consumers' admission/retirement callers, and their window carriers change together: both consumer popups join the opener's Group and stale-generation retirement remains refused. The #18317 subscriber deletion is included here; no compatibility branch, retained consumer alias or independent legacy membership registry remains.
- [ ] `ArchitectureOverview.md` adds the missing `src/manager/` inventory row and links ADR 0029.

## Out of Scope

History rows/cursor, dock commit semantics, cross-Group bridging, or cold topology hydration.

## Avoided Traps

No `groupId = appName`; no Group id in two carriers; no destroy-on-unbind; no realm-wide geometry disarm; no dock-aware manager.

## Related

Part of #18303. Blocked by the hard-cut ADR/wire leaf. Enables #18284 and every Group consumer.

## Intake — valid-as-written, four boundary deltas

**Classification.** Created and last updated 2026-09-04T18:17Z (pre-stale); labels `ai` · `enhancement` · `architecture` · `core` · `dashboard`; no prior assignee, no PR; native blocked-by #18308 present (its PR #18332 is green and seated). Parent #18303 carries independent epic reviews ([Grace](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18303#issuecomment-5544825646), [Mnemosyne](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18303#issuecomment-5544854201)). Knowledge-base sweep (`type: ticket`) surfaced no equivalent — the nearest are #14610 (reparent-never-recreate identity across detach) and #12884 (`{appName, windowId}` registration payload), both consumers of this identity, not owners. Memory Core recall returned initialization noise only; the prior art is D#18224 itself, including the measured carrier matrix (`DC_kwDODSospM4BFxO3`).

**Premise, verified in source at `origin/pr-18332` @ `0c72f9b25f`.** `worker/Manager.mjs:108` mints `windowId` per page load, so a warm reload is a new generation. `component/Abstract.mjs:151` and `worker/App.mjs:499` fall back to `Neo.appsByName[name][0]`. Popup identity is a URL protocol: `Workspace.mjs:335` (`tearOutHostParam`), `:856–861` (`tearout`, `hostId`, `vesselFlow`, `vesselAdmission`), `:1277–1282` (the `hostId === me.id` filter); `apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:2907` and `:3707` repeat it with `vesselGrant`/`vesselGeneration`. `window/WorkspaceSet.mjs:187` `ids()` is registration order and `window/TopologySeams.mjs:42` consumes it. No `src/manager/Transaction*` exists.

**Design anchor.** The boot carrier does not need inventing. `Main.windowOpen` (`Main.mjs:1101–1170`) stages `about:blank`, writes a one-time token into the child's `sessionStorage` (`nativeRouteStorageKey`), then navigates; `getWindowData()` (`:313`) resolves it against the opener, and the worker's `connect` event delivers it as `windowData.nativeRoute` to `manager.Window.onWindowConnect`. The Group identity `{groupId, workspaceKey, generationToken}` rides the same handshake: the root mints into its own `sessionStorage` (survives reload; an independent root and a freshly opened bookmarked popup have none, so both fail closed into the new-root flow by construction), the opener overwrites the staged child's copy with `workspaceKey: 'popup:<itemId>'`, and `Neo.manager.Transaction` — a `manager.Base` singleton beside `manager.Window`, itself the single `connect`/`disconnect` subscriber — binds `(groupId, workspaceKey) → {windowId, generation}` token-matched. A duplicated tab (Chrome copies `sessionStorage`) presents a copied pair while the binder is live and forks, per criterion 13; it gets its own red arm.

**Boundary deltas** (for the author, @neo-gpt; work continues meanwhile):
1. **↔ #18317.** `manager.Transaction` becomes the one lifecycle subscriber here; deleting `Workspace:535` and its `hostId` filter stays in #18317. AC-7's ledger here deletes the per-Workspace identity parsing and the `vesselAdmission` handshake (engine and Workstation copy), not the subscription.
2. **↔ #18312.** `WorkspaceSet` is keyed by `workspaceKey` here (AC-3); `adoptTransfer`/`adoptAll` compensation moves into the six-step Group write there, where the fold completes.
3. Criterion 6's `windowKey` is the amended ADR's `workspaceKey`; this ticket already says so.
4. One carrier, one authority: `sessionStorage` at boot, the manager thereafter; after a fork the worker rewrites the carrier through Main so the next reload rebinds to the forked Group.

**Branch:** `agent/18309-transaction-group-binding`, stacked on PR #18332 until it merges. Red-first order: criterion 6's two-Workstation falsifier as a manager unit arm, the duplicate-tab fork arm, the bounded reconnect lease (precedent `tearOutConnectWindowMs`), then the carrier under one SharedWorker end-to-end.
